line: The climb hurts most at the start. Higher up, it hurts less.
So on Kilimanjaro, a guide tells climbers: pole, pole. Slowly, slowly. No hurry.
Step by step, let no day pass without one small improvement.
In time, your mind stops flickering, like a flame where no wind blows.
Once your asana is steady, heat, cold, ups and downs cannot shake you.
At the hardest spot, the master cook slows down. One tiny cut does it.
Learn it deep, practise it long, and one day a breakthrough comes.
Keep climbing, until going up feels as easy as a boat drifting downstream.
But don't run. Go wisely and slowly: those who run fast stumble.
Hokusai said nothing he drew before 70 was good. Keep practising. You have time.
